problem: Existing test-time adaptation (TTA) methods for VLN treat online adaptation as a series of isolated, transient updates on one fixed parameter set, causing catastrophic forgetting of earlier adaptations and negative transfer to dissimilar scenes.
motivation: Deployed VLN agents face non-stationary shifts between scenes and within episodes, and scenes often recur or overlap. Past adaptation effort is wasted unless stored and reused, while feedback-driven TTA relying on foundation models is too slow for real-time use. The paper therefore treats adaptation knowledge as reusable assets that can be retrieved and recomposed.
key_idea: Store each adaptation as a compact asset (Fisher-weighted soft prompt, domain statistics, uncertainty), then build a training-free bridge to a new domain by projecting its statistics onto the convex hull of historical assets in closed form.
insight: Fisher-guided layer weighting is the biggest single contributor: it adds about +3.5 SR over decay weighting with nearest-asset retrieval. Convex-hull bridging beats hard nearest-asset retrieval, and only the full combination gives the large gains (val-unseen SR 46.98→56.92). Assets and bridge reinforce each other: coverage grows with library size, and the bridge gives a warm start that reduces later optimization. Shared assets also give training-free gains on new agents and across tasks.
method: Soft visual prompts: L=4 learnable tokens appended to the visual tokens before the cross-modal fusion transformer, so the frozen policy is modulated without parameter updates.

Multi-layer moment-matching alignment: prompts are optimized so per-layer mean/std of fused features (over candidate nodes) match precomputed source statistics (128 source samples), with a weighted sum across the M=4 fusion layers.

Fisher-guided weighting: layer weights alpha_l are updated by EMA (beta=0.1) from the normalized trace of the Fisher information of the policy w.r.t. layer features, a first-order proxy for the Hessian, to emphasize decision-relevant layers.

Triplet asset: each asset stores {prompt P*, feature statistics Gamma from the last fusion layer without prompt, uncertainty u = prediction entropy}; the library is capped at K_max=32, and new assets are merged with the nearest one by averaging.

Convex-hull bridge: mixture weights w minimize a Wasserstein-style statistics distance to the target plus lambda*sum u_j w_j^2 (lambda=0.4); the QP is solved in closed form via KKT (with clipping and renormalization if negative), and both prompts and statistics are interpolated with w.

Coverage gate: if the bridge prompt reduces the statistics discrepancy below tau·d0 (tau=0.7), it is used directly with no training; otherwise a new prompt is optimized for 50 steps, warm-started from the bridge, and added to the library.

setting.backbone: Pre-trained VLN policies HAMT, DUET, BEVBert, ETPNav (frozen weights; only soft prompts adapted at test time)
setting.model_size: Prompt library about 0.58 MB, <0.1% of the base model; base sizes not stated
setting.training_data: No extra training data; base policies use their standard training; source statistics come from 128 training trajectories; the test-time stream is adapted online (batch size 1, AdamW, lr 3e-3)
setting.observation: 360° panoramic RGB views with an online topological exploration graph; instruction text
setting.action_space: Discrete nav-graph node selection (DUET, HAMT, BEVBert); ETPNav for continuous R2R-CE via waypoints on a topological map

results: IDEA beats FSTTA and ReCAP on REVERIE, R2R and R2R-CE with four base policies. With DUET on REVERIE val-unseen, SR rises from 46.98 to 56.92 (ReCAP 54.74). It is the only method with gains on all metrics, and on R2R-CE val-unseen ETPNav SR rises from 57 to 59. It costs about 245-344 ms per episode, versus 5-8 s for feedback-driven FeedTTA/ATENA, while matching them on some unseen splits.
limitations: Evaluated only on single-agent benchmarks; multi-agent asset sharing and merging is untested.
Assets are tied to a specific model's feature space, so they cannot transfer across different architectures.
Gains on R2R-CE are small (about +2 SR) and everything is simulation only, with no real-robot test; the Wasserstein term is treated as a Euclidean/Gaussian approximation.
